breaks: /api/chat and /api/generate return 400 instead of 500 for non-LLM models — clients matching on 500 error responses get a different status code.
break_rulings.why: The HTTP status code changed from 500 to 400 for image, embedding, and reranking models on /api/chat and /api/generate.

breaks: The Noise backend upgraded from v0.12.1 to v0.15.0; existing image generation models run with the new backend on upgrade and may produce different output or fail.
break_rulings.why: A major backend version bump silently shipped with the release, changing inference behavior for every existing TheNoise model on upgrade.
These are bug fixes: /api/show now returns 200 for aliases (was 404), and /api/pull and /api/delete now correctly refuse aliases instead of acting on the target model.
The 500 to 400 change on /pull/variants is a bug fix — the old 500 was incorrect for a client error (unsupported files or invalid manifest).

evidence.blockers: One P0: the TheNoise 0.15.0 backend upgrade must be confirmed not to break existing image models. Several P1s require manual exercise of new API behavior (400 rejections, ollama CLI refusal), new GUI features (TheNoise recipe, SD.cpp upscaling), alias resolution, and Windows AMD iGPU memory detection. No showstoppers.
evidence.breaking_changes: API status codes changed from 500 to 400 on /api/chat and /api/generate for non-LLM models. The Noise backend version bumped from v0.12.1 to v0.15.0, which may change behavior for existing image models.
evidence.coverage: 17 commits reviewed across the range from v2026.47.1 to 4d0568a. All 29 to-dos are rated. No coverage gaps.
evidence.manual_testing: Ollama CLI integration (speech, decision, image model refusal, alias resolution), TheNoise 0.15.0 regression against existing models, new GUI custom model registration flow, and Windows AMD iGPU system-info and context sizing. These involve external tools, GUI interaction, or platform-specific hardware that CI does not exercise.
evidence.security: One security improvement merged: WebSocket credentials moved from URL query string to Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header (PR 4141). No new security concerns observed in this release.
